body.p: By way of summary, Claims 7-24 were pending in this application. In the present amendment, Applicant has amended the claims as shown above without prejudice or disclaimer. Accordingly, Claims 16-24 remain pending.
Rejections based on 35 U.S.C. @S 112

Claims 16-24 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph. Applicant has amended the claims for the purposes of clarification. Based at least on the amendments, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections.

Claims 16-24 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Chen (U.S. 2012/123222) in view of Zaleski (U.S. 7,945,457). The Office Action rejected the dependent claims based at least on the above cited references. Applicant respectfully traverses these rejections, the characterizations of the pending claims and the cited references and each and every implicit and explicit potential for reliance on Official Notice. Solely in the interest of expediting prosecution, Applicant has amended the independent claims as shown above. The dependent claims are addressed in the "Dependent Claims" section below.
Amended Claim 16 recites, among other things,
providing an option in a graphical user interface of the first software
presented on a display for a user to select the second software for a determination
of a health parameter;
receiving an indication that the second software was selected from the
option in the graphical user interface;

Chen fails to teach or suggest an ability for a user to select which parameters to be generated and how they are displayed on a user interface. Chen simply teaches a smart phone and an ability to download phone apps. There is no teaching about a user having an ability to select another software's "health parameter" that is different or not available from the first software, which might be the operating software, and the first software is responsible for determining physiological measurements. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection.

The dependent claims are patentable for the same reasons articulated above with respect to their independent claims. The dependent claims are also patentable because of the additional features recited therein.
No Disclaimers or Disavowals

Although the present communication may include alterations to the application or claims, or characterizations of claim scope or referenced art, Applicant is not conceding in this application that previously pending claims are not patentable over the cited references. Rather, any alterations or characterizations are being made to facilitate expeditious prosecution of this application. Applicant reserves the right to pursue at a later date any previously pending or other broader or narrower claims that capture any subject matter supported by the present disclosure, including subject matter found to be specifically disclaimed herein or by any prior prosecution. Accordingly, reviewers of this or any parent, child or related prosecution history shall not reasonably infer that Applicant has made any disclaimers or disavowals of any subject matter supported by the present application. Further, Applicant's arguments in favor of one independent claim should not be imputed to any other independent claim.

Applicant wishes to draw the Examiner's attention to the following co-pending applications of the present application's assignee.
By focusing on specific claims and claim recitations in the discussion above, Applicant does not intend to imply that other claim recitations are disclosed or rendered obvious by the art of record.
